newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE to set up match-making centres for nationals.
newsitem.headline: UAE to set up match-making centres for nationals.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates is planning to set up match-making centres across the oil-rich country to promote marriages among UAE nationals, the state-sponsored Marriage Fund said on Monday.

The fund, established three years ago to give financial aid to UAE men seeking to marry UAE women, wanted to expand its activities to cover more people in all seven of the emirates, the fund's Director-General Jamal al-Bah said in an interview published in the daily Khaleej Times.

"(Bah) said the centres would help UAE men and women find their life partners in an organised way," the paper said. "The match-making centre would enable both men and women to do this job in confidence."

Men wanting to use the centre's services would have to fill out an application in which they would describe the kind of woman they wanted to marry, the Khaleej Times said. Women could approach special women's committees at the centre, it added.
"When the right match is found, we will show the couple each other's photographs without revealing the names and if they like each other, we will arrange for them to meet," Bah said.
He said people had to realise the need for letting the bride and groom see each other before they got married, in accordance with Islamic sharia law, the paper said.

The Marriage Fund was set up by UAE President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan to encourage UAE men, often seeking foreign wives to avoid high traditional marriage and dowry costs, to marry local women.
UAE weddings are often costly affairs held in expensive hotels and involving lavish receptions.
The United Arab Emirates has given male citizens more than 560 million dirhams ($153 million) since the fund was established to promote marriages among UAE nationals.
But the fund has said figures showed more than a third of UAE men still took foreign wives, reporting on a trend it said was leading to a high divorce rate and a large number of unmarried UAE women.
